title: Debug: fix the syntax errors
prompt:
This program has three syntax errors. Fix them so it prints:

```
Python runs top to bottom
One error stops everything
```

Read the error message, fix the *first* problem only, and run again. Chasing all three at once is how you introduce a fourth.

starter_files.main.py:
print("Python runs top to bottom"
print('One error stops everything")
prnt("")

hints.text: Run it. The first error names a line number — start there and nowhere else.
Every opening parenthesis needs a matching closing one, and quotes must match in kind: open with `"`, close with `"`.
Line 3 is not a syntax error at all — it is a *name* error. Look carefully at the spelling of the function, and ask whether that line should exist.
Line 1 is missing `)`. Line 2 opens with `'` and closes with `"`. Line 3 misspells `print` and prints an empty line the expected output does not contain.

files.main.py:
print("Python runs top to bottom")
print("One error stops everything")

solution.explanation: Two syntax errors (unclosed call, mismatched quotes) and one line that should be deleted. The lesson: fix one error, re-run, repeat. Errors after the first are often phantoms caused by the first.

grader_config.expected_stdout:
Python runs top to bottom
One error stops everything
